items.title: Field: Name
items.text:
Alpha

The unique identifier of the Foundation:Kiva object. Referenced by a the "Outside Boundary Condition Object" field in a surface object.

items.title: Field: Initial Indoor Air Temperature
items.text:
Real Units: C

Indoor air temperature used for Kiva initialization (prior to warmup period). If left blank, indoor air temperature during initialization will be estimated based on zone setpoints.

items.title: Field: Interior Horizontal Insulation Material Name
items.text:
Object-List

A reference to a material object associated with the interior horizontal insulation. If left blank, no interior horizontal insulation will be used. Default: blank.

The following two fields define the placement of this material within Kiva's two-dimensional context and are illustrated in Figure 52.

Figure 52: Placement of interior horizontal insulation

items.title: Field: Interior Horizontal Insulation Depth
items.text:
Real Units: m Default: 0.0 Range: ≥ 0.0

Distance from the bottom of the slab to the top of interior horizontal insulation, in m. Generally, interior horizontal insulation is placed directly below the slab, and therefore, this value will generally be set to zero (as indicated in Figure 52). Required if Interior Horizontal Insulation Material Name is defined.

items.title: Field: Interior Horizontal Insulation Width
items.text:
Real Units: m Range: > 0.0

Extent of insulation as measured from the wall interior to the edge of interior horizontal insulation, in m. Required if Interior Horizontal Insulation Material Name is defined.

items.title: Field: Interior Vertical Insulation Material Name
items.text:
Object-List

A reference to a material object associated with the interior vertical insulation. If left blank, no interior vertical insulation will be used. Default: blank.

The following field defines the placement of this material within Kiva's two-dimensional context and are illustrated in Figure 53.

Figure 53: Placement of interior vertical insulation

items.title: Field: Interior Vertical Insulation Depth
items.text:
Real Units: m Range: > 0.0

Extent of insulation as measured from the wall top to the bottom edge of the interior vertical insulation, in m. Required if Interior Vertical Insulation Material Name is defined.

items.title: Field: Exterior Horizontal Insulation Material Name
items.text:
Object-List

A reference to a material object associated with the exterior horizontal insulation. If left blank, no exterior horizontal insulation will be used. Default: blank.

The following two fields define the placement of this material within Kiva's two-dimensional context and are illustrated in Figure 54.

Figure 54: Placement of exterior horizontal insulation

items.title: Field: Exterior Horizontal Insulation Depth
items.text:
Real Units: m Range: ≥ 0.0

Distance from the exterior grade to the top of exterior horizontal insulation, in m. Required if Exterior Horizontal Insulation Material Name is defined.

items.title: Field: Exterior Horizontal Insulation Width
items.text:
Real Units: m Default: 0.0 Range: ≥ 0.0

Extent of insulation as measured from the wall exterior to the edge of exterior horizontal insulation, in m. Required if Exterior Horizontal Insulation Material Name is defined.

items.title: Field: Exterior Vertical Insulation Material Name
items.text:
Object-List

A reference to a material object associated with the exterior vertical insulation. If left blank, no exterior vertical insulation will be used. Default: blank

The following field defines the placement of this material within Kiva's two-dimensional context and are illustrated in Figure 55.

Figure 55: Placement of exterior vertical insulation

items.title: Field: Exterior Vertical Insulation Depth
items.text:
Real Units: m Range: > 0.0

Extent of insulation as measured from the wall top to the bottom edge of the exterior vertical insulation, in m. Required if Exterior Vertical Insulation Material Name is defined.

items.title: Field: Wall Height Above Grade
items.text:
Real Units: m Default: 0.2 Range: ≥ 0.0

Distance from the exterior grade to the wall top, in m. Default: 0.2 m

Figures Figure 56 and Figure 57 illustrate the definition of both the "Wall Height Above Grade" and the following field, "Wall Depth Below Slab". If the top of foundation wall is flush with the ground then the "Wall Height Above Grade" is zero.

Figure 56: Definition of exterior grade and footing wall depth relative to the wall surface (for a basement foundation context)

Figure 57: Definition of exterior grade and footing wall depth relative to the wall surface (for a slab foundation context)

items.title: Field: Wall Depth Below Slab
items.text:
Real Units: m Default: 0.0 Range: ≥ 0.0

Distance from the slab bottom to the bottom of the foundation wall, in m. Default: 0.0 m

Extending the wall below the slab provides a coarse approximation of the foundation footing. Alternatively, one may use the fields "Footing Material Name" and "Footing Depth" to explicitly model the footing. Note, that explicit modeling of the footing requires a higher spatial discretization and, therefore, longer computation times.

items.title: Field: Footing Wall Construction Name
items.text:
Object-List

Defines the construction of the foundation footing wall for slab foundations where the foundation wall is not exposed to the zone (and has no zone surface to explicitly assign a construction).

By default, this is the same construction as any associated below-grade wall surfaces, or a 0.3 m wide poured concrete wall (conductivity = 1.95 W/m-K, density = 2240 kg/m3, specific heat = 900 J/kg-K).

items.title: Field: Footing Material Name
items.text:
Object-List

A reference to a material object associated with the foundation footing (typically some form of concrete). The thickness of this material is used to determine the width of the footing. If left blank, no footing will be used. Default: blank

The following field defines the placement of this material within Kiva's two-dimensional context and are illustrated in Figure 58.

Figure 58: Placement of footing

items.title: Field: Footing Depth
items.text:
Real Units: m Default: 0.3 Range: > 0.0

Top-to-bottom dimension of the footing (not to be confused with its depth in the ground). The width of the footing is defined by the material's thickness. Default: 0.3 m.

items.title: Field: Custom Block \<x> Material Name
items.text:
A reference to a material object associated with a custom block in the two-dimensional foundation context. The thickness of this material determines the width of the block.

Custom blocks can be used to represent solid materials in the two-dimensional context that are not otherwise covered by the fields above. Examples of this might include interior finishings and insulation (Figure 59) or backfill soil with different thermal properties (Figure 60).

Figure 59: Custom blocks representing interior batt insulation and dry wall

Figure 60: Custom block representing exterior backfill

If two or more custom blocks overlap, the final properties are determined by the higher block number (e.g., Custom Block 4 in the input object supersedes properties defined by Custom Block 2). All custom blocks properties are superseded by the elements shown in Figure 47.

The following fields defines the placement of this material within Kiva's two-dimensional context and are illustrated in Figure 61.

Figure 61: Placement of a custom block

items.title: Field: Custom Block \<x> Depth
items.text: Top-to-bottom dimension of the block downward. The default is the depth from the wall top to the top of the slab to facilitate interior constructions. Default: Slab depth

items.title: Field: Custom Block \<x> X Position
items.text: Position outward (+) or inward (-) relative to the foundation wall.

items.title: Field: Custom Block \<x> Z Position
items.text: Position downward (+) relative to the foundation wall top. Default: Wall top

items.title: Outputs
items.text:
Output for surfaces with a Foundation boundary condition type will include all opaque surface output variables except:

  • Surface Outside Face variables (since there is no "Outside Face")

  • Surface Heat Storage variables (since this definition depends on an "Outside Face")

  • Surface Internal Source Location Temperature (Kiva doesn't handle internal sources yet, but this is a possible future enhancement)

items.title: Foundation:Kiva:Settings
items.text: This object defines settings applied across all Kiva foundation calculations. This object is not required. If it is not defined, all defaults will be applied.

items.title: Field: Soil Conductivity
items.text:
Real Units: W/m-K Default: 1.73 Range: > 0.0

The thermal conductivity of the soil, in W/m-K. Default: 1.73 W/m-K.

items.title: Field: Soil Density
items.text:
Real Units: kg/m3 Default: 1842.0 Range: > 0.0

The bulk density of the soil, in kg/m3. Default: 1842 kg/m3.

items.title: Field: Soil Specific Heat
items.text:
Real Units: J/kg-K Default: 419.0 Range: > 0.0

The specific heat of the soil, in J/kg-K. Default: 419 J/kg-K

items.title: Field: Ground Solar Absorptivity
items.text:
Real Units: dimensionless Default: 0.9 Range: ≥ 0.0, ≤ 1.0

Solar absorptivity of the exterior grade surface. Default: 0.9.

items.title: Field: Ground Thermal Absorptivity
items.text:
Real Units: dimensionless Default: 0.9 Range: ≥ 0.0, ≤ 1.0

Long-wave absorptivity (emissivity) of the exterior grade surface. Default: 0.9.

items.title: Field: Ground Surface Roughness
items.text:
Real Units: m Default: 0.03 Range: > 0.0

The relief roughness of the exterior ground surface in m. Default: 0.03 m.

Estimates of surface roughnesses in m are shown in Table 1.

Example Surface Roughness [m] Concrete 0.002 Brick 0.003 Soil 0.005 Gravel 0.012 Grass 0.030

Table: Example Surface and Roughness

items.title: Field: Far-Field Width
items.text:
Real Units: m Default: 40.0 Range: > 0.0

The distance from the wall interior to the zero horizontal heat flux (i.e., adiabatic) far-field boundary, in m. This distance represents either the distance halfway between this foundation and a similar foundation of a neighboring building, or a distance adequately far from the foundation such that it is isolated from the effects of the boundary (typically >= 40 m). Default: 40 m.

items.title: Field: Deep-Ground Boundary Condition
items.text:
Choice Default: Autoselect Autoselect GroundWater ZeroFlux

Defines the type of boundary condition to apply at the Deep-Ground Depth. Options are:

  • ZeroFlux

  • GroundWater

  • Autoselect

ZeroFlux applies a zero vertical heat flux (i.e. adiabatic) boundary condition. GroundWater applies a constant temperature boundary condition, with a temperature equal to the average outdoor air dry-bulb temperature from the environment(s). Autoselect applies either boundary condition depending on the elevation of the building site (Williams and Williamson, 1989):

\[ d_{wt}=0.1022\cdot d_{elev} \]

If \(d_{wt} \le\) 40 m., the GroundWater boundary is applied at this depth, otherwise a ZeroFlux boundary is applied at 40 m. If the calculated ground water depth is shallower than any element of a foundation construction, then the GroundWater is applied at 1 m below the lowest element for that foundation.

Default: Autoselect.

items.title: Field: Deep-Ground Depth
items.text:
Real Units: m Default: Autocalculate Autocalculatable

The distance from the exterior grade to the deep ground boundary, in m. This distance represents either the distance to the ground water level, or a distance adequately far from the foundation such that it is isolated from the effects of the boundary (typically >= 40 m). Default 40 m, or the distance determined by the "Autoselect" Deep-Ground Boundary Condition. If the Deep-Ground Boundary Condition is set to "Autoselect", this field should be set to "Autocalculate". If the Deep-Ground Boundary Condition is not set to "Autoselect", but this field is set to "Autocalculate" (or allowed to default), an error will be issued.

Default: Autocalculate.

items.title: Field: Minimum Cell Dimension
items.text:
Real Units: m Default: 0.02 Range: > 0.0

The minimum cell dimension, in m, used in the Kiva discretization. Default: 0.02 m.

items.title: Field: Maximum Cell Growth Coefficient
items.text:
Real Units: dimensionless Default: 1.5 Range: ≥ 1.0

The maximum ratio of growth between neighboring cells in the direction away from the near-field area of interest. Default: 1.50.

items.title: Field: Simulation Timestep
items.text:
Choice Default: Hourly Hourly Timestep

This field allows the user to choose whether to calculate foundation loads on the zone timestep or at hourly intervals. Hourly intervals will allow for less overall computation time, but with less accuracy. Choices are "Hourly" and "Timestep". Default: Hourly

items.title: SurfaceProperty:ExposedFoundationPerimeter
items.text:
This object (currently only used in conjunction with Foundation:Kiva boundary conditions) defines the perimeter of a foundation floor that is exposed to the exterior environment through the floor. The user may either define the total exposed perimeter, the fraction of the total perimeter that is exposed, or individually define which segments of the floor surface perimeter are exposed. This object is required for any floor surface with a Foundation:Kiva boundary condition.

Figure 62 illustrates how the exposed perimeter is determined from a floor plan of the foundation level.

Some buildings may have neighboring zones with different foundation types. For example, a crawlspace next to a garage with a slab (Figure 63). The foundation wall in this case is NOT considered part of either floor's exposed perimeter, and should not reference a Foundation boundary condition. Kiva does not calculate heat flow between two zones through ground. In this case, it is best to approximate interior foundation wall using an Adiabatic Outside Boundary Condition.

Figure 62: Exposed foundation perimeter

Figure 63: Interior foundation wall

items.title: Field: Surface Name
items.text:
Object-List Required

Name of foundation floor surface object.

items.title: Field: Exposed Perimeter Calculation Method
items.text:
Choice Required BySegment ExposedPerimeterFraction TotalExposedPerimeter

Required key/choice field that tells which method to use to calculate the exposed foundation perimeter. Choices are:

  • TotalExposedPerimeter: Exposed perimeter is defined as an absolute distance in m. (The Total Exposed Perimeter field should be filled.)

  • ExposedPerimeterFraction: Exposed perimeter is defined as a fraction of the total floor perimeter. (The Exposed Perimeter Fraction field should be filled.) Note: This option works best when you are confident that the floor surface is completely exposed.

  • BySegment: Each segment of the floor polygon (corresponding to distance between each set of vertices) is defined as exposed ("Yes") or not exposed ("No") in an extensible list corresponding to the number of vertices in the floor polygon. Exposed perimeter is defined as the sum of all exposed segment lengths. (The Surface Segment \<x> Exposed fields should be filled.) Note: The number of segments identified in this object must match the number of vertices in the corresponding surface object.

items.title: Field: Total Exposed Perimeter
items.text:
Real Units: m Range: ≥ 0.0

Total perimeter that is exposed in m.

items.title: Field: Exposed Perimeter Fraction
items.text:
Real Units: dimensionless Default: 1.0 Range: ≥ 0.0, ≤ 1.0

Fraction of the total perimeter that is exposed. Default 1.0

items.title: Field: Surface Segment \<x> Exposed
items.text: Surface Segment \<x> is the perimeter between the \<x>th and (\<x>+1)th vertices.

items.title: SurfaceConvectionAlgorithm:Inside:AdaptiveModelSelections

This object is only needed to make changes to the default model selections for any or all of the surface categories. This object is for the inside face, the side of the surface facing a thermal zone.

items.title: SurfaceConvectionAlgorithm:Inside:UserCurve
items.text: This object is used to describe a custom model equation for surface convection heat transfer coefficients. If more than one curve is referenced, or non-blank, then they are all used, and the result is the simple addition of all the curve results.

items.title: Field: Name
items.text:
Alpha

Unique name of input object.

items.title: Field: Reference Temperature for Convection Heat Transfer
items.text:
Choice AdjacentAirTemperature MeanAirTemperature SupplyAirTemperature

This field controls the nature of the reference temperature used with convection coefficient when calculating the heat flow at the surface. Select one of the three choices: MeanAirTemperature, AdjacentAirTemperature, SupplyAirTemperature. MeanAirTemperature is the typical application for the classic convection model used with the complete mixing of room air. AdjacentAirTemperature applies when used with Roomair models that account for temperature variations within the zone air and directs the model to use the temperature near the surface rather than the average for the entire zone. SupplyAirTemperature directs the model to use the supply air conditions for the heat transfer conditions.

items.title: Field: Hc Function of Temperature Difference Curve Name
items.text:
Object-List

This field contains the name of separate performance curve or table object that describes h\(_{c}\), the convection coefficient, as a function of temperature difference. The curve's "x" is absolute value of delta-T (Surface temperature minus air temperature, (C))

items.title: Field: Hc Function of Temperature Difference Divided by Height Curve Name
items.text:
Object-List

This field contains the name of separate performance curve or table object that describes h\(_{c}\), the convection coefficient, as a function of temperature difference divided by height. The curve's "x" is absolute value of delta-T/Height (Surface temp minus Air temp)/(vertical length scale), (C/m). For an inside face, the vertical length scale is the zone's interior height.

items.title: Field: Hc Function of Air Change Rate Curve Name
items.text:
Object-List

This field contains the name of separate performance curve or table object that describes h\(_{c}\), the convection coefficient, as a function of air change rate. The curve's "x" is mechanical ACH (Air Changes per hour from mechanical air system), (1/hr)

items.title: Field: Hc Function of Air System Volume Flow Rate Divided by Zone Perimeter Length Curve Name
items.text:
Object-List

This field contains the name of separate performance curve or table object that describes h\(_{c}\), the convection coefficient, as a function of air change rate divided perimeter scale. Curve's "x" is mechanical system air flow rate (m\(^{3}\)/s) divided by zone's length along exterior walls (m).

items.title: SurfaceConvectionAlgorithm:Outside:UserCurve
items.text: This object is used to describe a custom model equation for surface convection heat transfer coefficients. If more than one curve is referenced, or non-blank, then they are all used and the result is the simple addition of all the curve results.

items.title: Field: Name
items.text:
Alpha

Unique name of input object.

items.title: Field: Wind Speed Type for Curve
items.text:
Choice Default: HeightAdjust HeightAdjust ParallelComponent ParallelComponentHeightAdjust WeatherFile

This field specifies what sort of wind velocity data should be used in when evaluating the curve in the following field. There are for key choice options. "WeatherFile" directs using the unmodified value from the epw file or design weather data. "HeightAdjust" uses the value from the epw file modified for height above ground, as determined by the z coordinate, using the site terrain and weather station information. "ParallelComponent" uses the value from the epw file modified to take just the velocity component that is parallel to the surface. "ParallelComponentHeightAdjust" uses the height adjusted wind velocity and then computes the parallel component.

items.title: Field: Hf Function of Wind Speed Curve Name
items.text:
Object-List

items.title: SurfaceProperty:ConvectionCoefficients
items.text:
The convection coefficients of each surface, both exterior and interior, are automatically calculated during EnergyPlus execution. These calculations are "governed" by other objects such as the SurfaceConvectionAlgorithm:Inside (overall default), the Zone object's field called Zone Inside Convection Algorithm (Zone Default), the and the SurfaceConvectionAlgorithm:Outside (overall default), and/or the Zone object's field called Zone Outside Convection Algorithm (Zone Default). Usually, that will be enough flexibility for most users. However, if you need to match pre-existing convection coefficients (from another program) or are trying to match a test suite of results, you may wish to use the "override" convection coefficients in the following object. This object allows for a single surface to be given specific convection coefficients.

Note that using these in conjunction, in particular, the "Simple" option on either the Outside Convection Algorithm or the Zone Outside Convection Algorithm field will result in a combined coefficient regardless of choice chosen here.

Note that surfaces with "SurfaceProperty:OtherSideCoefficients" cannot use this object with the "outside" coefficient -- attempting to do so will cause a severe error; SurfaceProperty:OtherSideCoefficients surfaces can apply an "inside" coefficient. And, surfaces with "Ground" exposure do not use the "outside" coefficient that might be supplied here. Note, too, that some lower boundaries are used regardless by certain surface types (i.e. Window) or certain algorithm types.

items.title: SurfaceProperty:ConvectionCoefficients:MultipleSurface
items.text:
The convection coefficients of each surface, both outside and inside, are automatically calculated during EnergyPlus execution. These calculations are "governed" by other objects such as the Inside Convection Algorithm (overall default) and the Zone Inside Convection Algorithm (Zone Default) and the Outside Convection Algorithm (overall default) and/or the Zone Outside Convection Algorithm (Zone Default). Usually, that will be enough flexibility for most users. However, if you need to match pre-existing convection coefficients (from another program) or are trying to match a test suite of results, you may wish to use the "override" convection coefficients in the following object. This object is similar to the preceding "ConvectionCoefficients" object but allows multiple surfaces to be assigned a type with one object entry.

Note that using these in conjunction, in particular, the "Simple" option on either the Outside Convection Algorithm or the Zone Outside Convection Algorithm field will result in a combined coefficient regardless of choice chosen here.

Note that surfaces with "SurfaceProperty:OtherSideCoefficients" cannot use this object with the "outside" coefficient -- attempting to do so will ignore OSC surfaces during a multiple surface "apply"; SurfaceProperty:OtherSideCoefficients surfaces can apply an "inside" coefficient. And, surfaces with "Ground" exposure do not use the "outside" coefficient that might be supplied here. Note, too, that some lower boundaries are used regardless by certain surface types (i.e. Window) or certain algorithm types.

items.title: Convection Coefficient Application Hierarchy
items.text:
Ultimate flexibility and possibly ultimate user confusion can result from the convection coefficient possibilities in EnergyPlus. The objects that control how convection models are assigned to individual surfaces  are:

  • SurfaceConvectionAlgorithm:Inside

  • SurfaceConvectionAlgorithm:Outside

  • Zone, Field: Zone Inside Convection Algorithm

  • Zone, Field: Zone Outside Convection Algorithm

  • SurfaceProperty:ConvectionCoefficients

  • SurfaceProperty:ConvectionCoefficients:MultipleSurface

General to Specific, they are assigned in this order:

Objects/Description Action SurfaceConvectionAlgorithm:* Assigns for all surfaces in the run. Zone, Fields: Zone * Convection Algorithm Trumps global assignment and assigns for all surfaces in Zone. SurfaceProperty:...:MultipleSurfaces Trumps above and assigns for specific types of surfaces. Two Multiple Surface Assignments overlapping (such as AllExteriorSurfaces vs AllExteriorWalls) Order in IDF is now important. Whichever is first gets the cookie and the second gets a warning. Specific Surface Assignment Trumps all Above.

Table: Convection Coefficient Assignment Hierarchy

There are additional objects that provide fine control over the models that get assigned.

  • SurfaceConvectionAlgorithm:Inside:AdaptiveModelSelections

  • SurfaceConvectionAlgorithm:Outside:AdaptiveModelSelections

  • SurfaceConvectionAlgorithm:Inside:UserCurve

  • SurfaceConvectionAlgorithm:Outside:UserCurve

items.text:
Outputs for the User Supplied Convection Coefficients appear as values in the Surface Output Variables (Surface Inside Face Convection Heat Transfer Coefficient and Surface Outside Face Convection Heat Transfer Coefficient). What the program expects to use is shown in the Surface Details report (Output:Surfaces:List, Details;)

When EnergyPlus is set to Display Advanced Variables (Output:Diagnostics, DisplayAdvancedVariables;), then additional output variables are available that indicate the status of convection modeling by identifying which models are in effect at a given time.  The adaptive convection algorithms may switch between models over time and the following output variables provide a way to monitor this behavior.  These outputs are integer codes and the integer values are explained in tables.

items.title: SurfaceProperties:VaporCoefficients
items.text: Advanced/Research Usage: The internal and external vapor transfer coefficients that are used by the CombinedHeatAndMoistureFiniteElement model are automatically calculated during EnergyPlus execution using information on the convection coefficients. However it is sometimes useful to be able to "override" the calculation and set fixed values of vapor transfer coefficient for a single surface. These coefficients are only used by the CombinedHeatAndMoistureFiniteElement model and will be ignored by other solution algorithms.

items.text:
